thesis: AI may structure and prepare evidence, but evidence integrity, case authority, source metadata and external legal actions remain independently inspectable and human-controlled.

evidence.claim: Court-Prep model output cannot switch the active case or invent archive network targets; deterministic wrappers own those authorities.
The Court-Prep runtime is case-bound and network archive targets are evidence-bound, but a portable capability-policy contract is not yet applied across every SafeVoice agent/MCP surface.
The Court-Prep agent blocks model-selected cross-case pivots before handlers execute; full production multi-tenant isolation remains separately unproven.
An approval checkpoint is required before external legal action.
Evidence receives SHA-256 hashes, timestamps, source metadata and browser-side integrity verification.
Court-Prep case scope and archive egress are deterministic and fail closed, but broader protected-scope/exfiltration coverage across every runtime surface remains incomplete.
The agent runtime has explicit tools, iteration limits and audit records.
Evidence hashes/source metadata and bounded agent audit records support inspectable review.
No complete SBOM, signing or third-party supply-chain assurance claim is published.
Two dedicated compromised-model security regressions prove zero handler/network impact for cross-case and model-invented archive-target attacks.
The current repository does not claim production security monitoring or incident-response evidence.

residualRisks: The existing 35-case product evaluation remains separate from dedicated adversarial security evidence.

The new regressions cover the reachable Court-Prep case-switch and archive-egress paths; broader MCP, indirect prompt-injection, protected-scope and full multi-tenant attack coverage remains incomplete.
Production multi-tenant isolation, supply-chain integrity and security monitoring remain unproven.
Qualified human review remains required before any external legal action.
